hitl_conditions: Operator policy in the Admission Controller sets autonomy: manual review of every incoming update, whitelisting (safety-critical firmware auto-applied, process-parameter changes need explicit approval), or fully autonomous AI agent; process compensation and federated propagation run without operator intervention.
key_finding: Analytical framework: each fabrication node's Cognitive Gateway hosts a digital-twin nominal model whose twin gap trains a GP/neural-network disturbance estimator that automatically corrects control inputs; federated learning propagates corrections. FOSS governance provides redundancy, substitutability and informational persistence, absorbing supply chain (vendor lock-in), regulatory and process disturbances without central control.

quotes.text: node-local digital twins—each hosting a machine learning (ML) disturbance estimator—provide local adaptive compensation without centralised data aggregation. A defining property of the architecture is automatic improvement propagation: learned corrections distribute via federated learning to structurally similar nodes without operator intervention

The third disturbance class addresses supply chain disruptions arising from proprietary vendor actions: firmware lock-down, component discontinuation, or deliberate incompatibility introduced to capture market share.

quotes.text: It is software running on the node’s co-located compute substrate, automating what an experienced human operator would otherwise do manually: diagnosing process drift, fitting compensation models, and closing the gap between nominal design intent and physical output.

At the other extreme, a manual operator reviews and approves each incoming change before it is applied to the local node. Between these poles, semi-autonomous configurations allow operators to whitelist categories of updates
Second, the ML compensation layer is treated as a conceptual component of the framework; no specific learning algorithms are implemented or benchmarked.
